title: Food As Medicine
subtitle: A thINc360 dispatch
text:
Greetings readers! I’m reporting live from the thINc360 conference where the focus is on food as medicine. For my health professional readers, the following link gets you… 5.5 AMA CME category one credits…it’s a learning module to train all health professionals on the basics of food as medicine. (Free with code whc22)

I’ve written before about Obesity as a disease. I’ve been obese. I had one blood test worth of diabetes. I don’t have diabetes as an illness anymore. It is not just because of “eating healthy” for me—yes, it includes semglutide—for me, anyway. This isn’t an easy fix and comes with significant drawbacks.

We developed ultra processed food as Americans to avoid famine. These ultra processed foods account for over 89% of added sugars.

Point 1: Sugar is Poison.

I can see the historical domino sugar factory from my bathroom window.

Before cane sugar was brought to Europe—from slave plantations in Brazil 400 years ago, sweetened was expensive and rare. We had dates and honey, easily accessible. Sugar could utilize slave labor to be made cheaply— the cruelty was the cradle for our sugar sweetened culture.

This episode of through line is a phenomenal history of sweetness…

There was a relentless sales pitch. We embedded sweetness into our language—equated as good. Have you called your lover “sweetie?” That is sugar propaganda we simple forget about. “I’m sweet on you.” Valentine’s Day? Sweet chocolates. It’s everywhere.

Remarkable piles of money are made by Big Sugar. South Park’s the end of Obesity on this topic is hilarious and crucial viewing, because sugar and pharma are now no longer in sync. GLP-1s are a shot across the bow…Qua South Park:

drugs for the rich people,

body positivity for poor people

How big of a deal is this financial flywheel? Just looking at sweetened drinks consumed at home in billions:

That doesn’t count Big Oats…(Quaker is owned by PepsiCo…so it’s the same thing…Steel Cut Oats don't need to be poisoned by sugar!). Diabetes medicines are a huge business:

Food, sleep, and loving community are the basis of health—and the opposite of those is the basis of disaster.

I'm leaving aside “targeted and serious” interventions like nutritional ketosis here, but it is worth learning about for serious mental illness.
